target.title: fix(feishu): add chunk-idle timeout to inbound media download
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a stalled Feishu (Lark SDK) inbound media download body blocks the channel's agent-reply workflow indefinitely because the underlying Node.js `Readable` async iterator never settles on empty/stalled streams. Additionally preserves the established Feishu timeout policy: the per-chunk idle timeout is derived from the canonical `resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs()` resolver (respecting `OPENCLAW_FEISHU_HTTP_TIMEOUT_MS` env var, account config, and default) instead of a hardcoded 30s value.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Wrap each `AsyncIterable.next()` call in `Promise.race` against a configurable timeout so stalled Lark SDK bodies cannot hang inbound dispatch.
- **Do NOT `await` iterator.return()** in the finally block — Node Readable async-iterator `return()` hangs when the underlying source is stalled (waits for a `readable` event that never fires). Instead, explicitly **destroy** the source on timeout so the underlying Readable (and its HTTP resource) close, then call `iterator.return()` without awaiting.
- Thread the canonical Feishu timeout (`resolveConfiguredHttpTimeoutMs`) from `saveMessageResourceFeishu()` through `saveMessageResourceWithType()` → `saveFeishuResponseMedia()` → `saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout()`, so the per-chunk idle deadline respects the user's configured HTTP timeout policy.
- ClawSweeper Maintainer option 1 (**Cancel and prove the source**): implemented — timeout path calls `destroySource()`; focused + HTTP loopback proofs assert `destroyed=true` and server-side connection close.
- No new config/env surface. The timeout inherits the existing Feishu HTTP timeout policy.

Collision check: searched open PRs for "feishu chunk-idle timeout media download stall"; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

- **Before**: A stalled Lark SDK media stream (TCP accepted, headers received, body never produces chunks) would hang inbound dispatch indefinitely — no agent reply, no error logged.
- **After**: Stream times out after the resolved idle period with `FeishuInboundMediaTimeoutError`. The underlying source Readable is explicitly destroyed so the HTTP resource closes. Normal progressing streams are unaffected.

## Verification

- Exact head: `a494f81c84b4d0a471fb3a7fca2e6c2329615a30`
- `oxfmt` on touched Feishu media idle files — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed; exit 0.
- Focused tests:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.test.ts extensions/feishu/src/media-chunk-idle.proof.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 Test Files  3 passed (3)
      Tests  46 passed (46)
```

- Mutation check: removing `destroySource(source)` on timeout makes the HTTP loopback assertion `server_close=true` / `destroyed=true` fail; restoring passes.
- Rebased onto latest `origin/main` before this proof refresh.

## Evidence

Exact commands + observed output are under **Real behavior proof** below (HTTP loopback local-server boundary). Vitest suite above includes the same HTTP `IncomingMessage` case in CI-discoverable form.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: chunk-idle timeout on stalled Feishu/Lark-like media download stream, with source destroy + HTTP connection close, preserving canonical Feishu HTTP timeout policy.
Real environment tested: Node 22, production `saveMediaStream` / `saveMediaStreamWithIdleTimeout`, local `node:http` server on `127.0.0.1` (headers flushed, body stalled), Node `IncomingMessage` Readable — same boundary Lark SDK `getReadableStream()` returns. No live Feishu credentials.
Exact commands run:

```bash
node --import tsx extensions/feishu/src/proof-feishu-media-chunk-idle.mts
```

Observed output after fix:

```text
node=v22.22.0
head=a494f81c84b4d0a471fb3a7fca2e6c2329615a30

[case 1] negative control — stalled HTTP body without idle wrap
  ok: stalled HTTP Readable without idle wrap stays pending (>300ms)
  info: outcome=still-pending wait_ms=301 without_idle_wrap=true

[case 2] positive control — stalled HTTP body with idle wrap
  ok: timed out (not resolved)
  ok: error is FeishuInboundMediaTimeoutError
  ok: timeout fires within 3s
  ok: timeout fires after the idle budget
  ok: source Readable is destroyed after timeout
  ok: server observed client/connection close after destroy
  info: elapsed_ms=86 timed_out=true destroyed=true server_close=true chunkTimeoutMs=80

[case 3] valid response — progressing HTTP body
  ok: saved media size matches input
  ok: contentType preserved
  info: size=4 contentType=image/jpeg timed_out=false

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

Evidence:
- Negative control: stalled HTTP body without idle wrap stays pending (`outcome=still-pending`, wait_ms≈300)
- Positive control: idle wrap rejects with `FeishuInboundMediaTimeoutError`, `destroyed=true`, and `server_close=true` (client tear-down observed by the local server)
- Valid path: progressing HTTP JPEG body saves (`size=4 timed_out=false`)
- Vitest HTTP case asserts the same destroy + server close contract at exact head

What was not tested: Live Feishu/Lark cloud media download, real bot token, Desktop message dispatch. Proof is controlled local-server at the Node Readable/HTTP boundary the SDK exposes.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low/Medium. New post-header idle failure boundary reuses the existing Feishu HTTP timeout resolver (no new env/config). Progressing streams unchanged. Timeout now destroys the source Readable so sockets do not accumulate after releasing the agent workflow. AI-assisted.
